conviction_note: The evidence is mostly peer and macro proxies. They point to a strong Industrial (Motion) quarter, a NAPA quarter in line with or soft against an already-lowered auto guide, and restructuring savings that make the $2.04-2.05 bar beatable. That gives a print a little above the bar (print_vs_bar about +0.8% on revenue, about +2% on EPS). This name sold its Q2 beat (-2.68% close, about -7% intraday) on auto caution, and the December 8-9 investor days probably defer any 2027 or standalone framework. So the reaction is a weak lean (p_up 54) on an abs move of 4.5, between the 2.68 median and the indicative 7.0 implied, which carries a 61% ATM spread. impact_sum +0.3 and impact_scaled +0.36 agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 adj EPS $2.04-2.05 and revenue $6.49-6.50B: Benzinga consensus ($2.05 / $6.49B, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GPC/earnings-forecasts) and Tickerleague, 6 analysts ($2.04, range $1.98-2.12 / $6.5B, https://tickerleague.com/companies/GPC/estimates). Two sources agree. Earnings Whispers carries $2.10 / $6.47B (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/GPC), so the whisper sits above. Year-ago Q3 2025: adj EPS $1.98, sales $6.26B. Company FY2026 guide: adj EPS $7.50-8.00, total sales +3-5.5%, NA Automotive +2.5-4.5% (cut from 3-5%), International +5-8% (raised), Industrial +3-6% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040987/000004098726000031/gpc-earnq22026.htm). FY consensus about $7.69 (MarketBeat).
positioning_check: Short interest 6.6% of float with 3.8 days to cover as of the 2026-07-15 settlement (tapeboard, from FINRA files: https://tapeboard.com/stock/GPC/short-squeeze/). Equibles shows 2.42 DTC at 2026-03-13 (https://equibles.com/stocks/gpc/shortinterest). No October settlement found. Not crowded. Baseline 25d skew is +0.04 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.24 (call-heavy but total OI only 2,868), ATM IV 44% against 19% 20d realised, event-implied 7.0%, ATM spread 61% of mid (indicative only). Run-up +5.36% over 20d and +2.79% over 5d; 10.7% below the 52w high, which was set around the July O'Reilly-bid spike. Insider Form 4s since July are tax withholding only (code F).

findings.finding: Motion's peers and the industrial series all ran hot through Q3 after GPC last spoke on 2026-07-21. Fastenal Q3 daily sales +15.5% (September +14.4%), Applied Industrial organic about +7% through mid-August with Engineered Solutions orders up mid-20s in July, and the ISM September PMI 54.5, a 9th straight month of expansion with prices at 77.9. Motion's Q3 comp likely runs at or above Q2's +6.1% (H1 +5.0%), against a full-year Industrial sales guide of +3-6% that was left unchanged in July. Motion is about 37% of sales and 13.1% EBITDA margin; the read is net of a flat-to-soft NA auto (separate finding).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: Industrial comp +6.1% and EBITDA +9.8% beat, yet the stock closed -2.68% (about -7% intraday) because the auto outlook dominated (https://www.itiger.com/hant/news/2653274581). Industrial strength has not by itself carried a print this year.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: industrial distributors are public and GPC is +5.4% over 20 days. What is not visible: the Industrial guide is still +3-6% and consensus revenue of $6.49-6.50B implies only about +3.7% total growth. If the market had priced a Motion raise, consensus would sit above $6.5B and the stock would not be 10.7% below its high.
findings.independence: Applied Industrial FY27 guide and July/August trend (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109563/000010956326000031/a8k8132026releaseexhibit991.htm, 2026-08-13); ISM September 2026 PMI 54.5 (https://www.ismworld.org/supply-management-news-and-reports/reports/ism-pmi-reports/pmi/september/, 2026-10-01). GPC's own Q2 call said July 'picked up where June left off' for Motion (https://www.webull.com/news/15265626932274176). Three different documents.

findings.finding: US auto-parts peers that reported after GPC's July call show weak DIY, strong commercial and a June trough. AutoZone domestic comp +1.6% for the 16 weeks to 2026-08-29 (DIY -0.6%, commercial +8.6%, August +2.1%, Q1 FY27 total comps guided about flat). Advance Auto Q2 comp -0.5% to 2026-07-18, with DIY weakening in the final four weeks. NAPA Q2 had commercial about +4% and retail about -3%, and its full-year NA Automotive sales guide was already cut to +2.5-4.5%. NAPA's Q3 comp likely runs low single digits, in line with the lowered guide, with risk at its low end; peers' commercial at +8-10% implies continued NAPA share loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NA auto is the line this stock trades on: Q2 2026 lowered the NA auto range and the stock fell about 7% intraday despite an EPS beat; Feb 2026 print -14.56%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the July guide cut already embeds softness. What is unpriced is whether NAPA independents and US comps hold +2.5% for the year. A market pricing a second cut would show put skew rather than +0.04 and a 20d run-up below zero.
findings.independence: Advance Auto Q2 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158449/000119312526357755/aap-ex99_1.htm, 2026-08). O'Reilly Q2 comp +6.0% with pro about +10% (https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/07/29/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-second-quarter-2026-results/) points the other way on the market and the same way on share.

findings.finding: Gasoline stayed near $4 through Q3 (about $4.15 national average at Labor Day 2026, crude near $90 on Strait of Hormuz volatility, AP $4 on 2026-07-20). That sits at or above the conditions behind GPC's July guide of $20-30M incremental H2 fuel and freight cost (Q2 Iran-conflict EBITDA hit $16M, nearly all in Automotive) and its caution on consumer sentiment. The guide likely lands at the upper end of the cost range: about $0.05-0.08 per share over H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 call's fuel/Iran caution coincided with the -7% intraday drop on 2026-07-21.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: management named the headwind in July and gas prices are the most public series there is. Only the step from the guided $20-30M to the top of it is new, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: AP via ABC, gas back to $4 on 2026-07-20 (https://abcnews.com/Business/wireStory/us-gas-prices-hit-average-4-gallon-us-134908471). Same macro series, so not independent of the cause. The source is a snippet-quality blog figure; AAA was not read directly.

findings.finding: Restructuring savings ramp in H2: the 2026 plan targets $100-125M of benefit, $55M was delivered by June ($30M in Q2, about $0.16/share), leaving $45-70M (about $0.12-0.19/share) for H2. Against a Q3 2025 base of $1.98, the $2.04-2.05 bar needs only +3% growth, so the quarter clears the bar unless cost inflation (health care +15%, fuel) eats most of the savings. This is inside what the company guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 adj EPS $2.15 beat about $2.10 consensus, and the stock still fell (-2.68% close). EPS beats have not been paid on this name in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the company's guide, so the bar should embed it. What would show it unpriced is consensus at or below the year-ago growth rate, and $2.04-2.05 against $1.98 is close to that. The +3% implied growth sits below H1's restructuring-aided pace.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K adjusted EPS reconciliation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040987/000004098726000031/gpc-earnq22026.htm) is the same company source. Nothing independent.

findings.finding: LKQ's European organic parts revenue fell 12.6% in Q2 2026 on a German ERP rollout, and LKQ cut its 2026 guide mainly for Europe; Germany was only back above 85% of normal run-rate in late July. GPC said in July that the UK and Germany were notably improving and raised its International Automotive sales guide to +5-8%. A share-gain tailwind for GPC Europe in Q3 is plausible but unconfirmed by GPC.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: International was raised in July and was not what moved the stock; Europe has been a secondary line.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy transmission that nobody has quantified for GPC; previews do not mention it. If priced, consensus International comps would be above the +0.6% Q2 pace, and the consensus revenue bar does not suggest that.
findings.independence: GPC Q2 call, UK/Germany improvement and the International guide raise (https://www.webull.com/news/15265626932274176). Different company, same direction.

findings.finding: GPC's 10-Q says its importer-of-record exposure to the invalidated IEEPA tariffs is under 0.5% of total purchases, and that refund claims were submitted in Q2 and were immaterial. Unlike Advance Auto (about $0.31/share of tariff refunds in Q2) and AutoZone (about 145bp of gross margin from refunds), GPC has no refund cushion coming in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No GPC history; peers' refund-aided quarters are the only comparison.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in the 10-Q, so the bar should exclude refunds. The only risk is a reader extrapolating peers' refund-boosted margins; consensus at +3% EPS growth shows no such extrapolation.
findings.independence: AAP Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158449/000119312526357755/aap-ex99_1.htm) and AZO Q4 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866787/000117184326006159/exh_991.htm) show what peers received.

findings.finding: The 2026-09-09 8-K set separate GPC and Motion investor days for December 8 and 9, 2026, named Court Carruthers CEO-elect of the automotive company and Will Stengel CEO of Motion, and kept the separation on track for Q1 2027. Standalone targets and any 2027 framework are therefore likely held for December rather than given on this call, which lowers the odds of a guide-driven outsized move. The leadership naming also signals the spin path over the O'Reilly bid.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Feb 2026 print (-14.56%) carried the separation announcement and a new-year guide; a Q3 print without a new-year guide has run smaller (Oct 2025 +2.05%).
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 2026-09-09. It bears on the size of the move, not its sign, which is why it is sized 0 and shows up in abs_move_pct.

findings.finding: Bloomberg reported on 2026-07-02 that O'Reilly made a $10B+ cash bid for GPC's automotive unit (shares reportedly jumped about 13%). On the 2026-07-21 call management said it is 'not currently in discussions with any competitor', and on 2026-09-09 it named a CEO-elect for the standalone auto company. Any residual takeover premium is exposed if the call repeats spin-only.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The bid report moved the stock about +13% on 2026-07-02 (single outlet). The July call's denial coincided with the -7% intraday drop.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced after the July denial and the September leadership 8-K; the stock is below its July spike high. The residual is the call Q&A, which could cut either way.
findings.independence: GPC Q2 call transcript, 'not currently in discussions' (https://www.webull.com/news/15265626932274176); shares the September 8-K with the investor-day finding.

findings.finding: GPC filed an automatic shelf (S-3ASR) on 2026-10-16 registering an indeterminate amount of common, preferred and debt, with proceeds for 'general corporate purposes'. It is the third in a three-year cadence (2020-10-23, 2023-10-20, 2026-10-16), so it is a routine renewal and not an offering, though it leaves room for the separation capital structure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No reaction history; prior renewals carried no print reaction of their own.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public. Sized 0 because the money buys nothing specific: an expiring 2023 shelf replaced on schedule.
findings.independence: EDGAR full-text search shows the prior S-3ASR filings on 2020-10-23 and 2023-10-20 (https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22automatic%20shelf%22&ciks=0000040987&forms=S-3ASR).

outside_window.finding: GPC and Motion investor days on 2026-12-08 and 2026-12-09, where standalone targets and capital structure are expected.
O'Reilly Q3 2026 results (due about 2026-10-22), the next read on commercial share against NAPA.

searched_and_found_nothing: Analyst rating or price-target changes in September and October 2026 (latest found: Fintel 2026-08-28 average target $145.55; no dated Sept/Oct actions)
Any report that the O'Reilly bid was formally rejected or revived after July 2026
Public Form 10 for Motion on EDGAR (confidential filing only)
Insider open-market buys or sells since July 2026 (Form 4s are tax withholding or director quarterly filings)

GPC-specific tariff-refund amounts beyond the 10-Q 'not material' language

baseline_tension: Skew is flat (+0.04) and the stock has run up 5.4% over 20 days on what is probably industrial strength, so the mild positive lean agrees with the tape and is likely partly priced. This name's habit of selling beats on auto caution pulls p_up toward 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest) and lesson 1 (this name sold its Q2 beat): the Motion finding went from +1.0 to +0.8.
Lesson 6 (inside what the company guided): the restructuring-savings finding went from +0.4 to +0.3.
Lesson 5 (proxy, snippet-only source): the fuel finding went from -0.4 to -0.3.
Lesson 1 (reaction veto): p_up went from 55 to 54; abs_move_pct stays at 4.5.

Lessons 4 and 7 left standing: the shelf was checked as a routine renewal (0); short interest of 6.6% is not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk for a squeeze. The bar has two agreeing sources, so no cap.
